scout.productSummary: A 28-day demand forecast for every product in one Walmart store (CA_1, 3,049 item series), built on the real Kaggle M5 data with an evaluation harness designed to be honest. ALREADY EXISTS: m5-download fetches the four M5 files from a pinned HuggingFace mirror and refuses any file whose sha256 differs from provenance/m5_data.json; m5-features builds 52 leakage-tested features (sales inputs at least 28 days old, tests/test_leakage.py); m5-backtest runs six models (seasonal-naive, linear regression, Ridge, a logistic hurdle model, LightGBM and XGBoost with Tweedie loss and in-fold tuning) on 3 walk-forward folds scored with the competition's WRMSSE and writes results/metrics.json; m5-plots and m5-explain draw the forecast plot, exact TreeSHAP for both boosted models and a model-free SNAP-day lift; m5-writeup rewrites every number in README.md, docs/RESULTS.md and docs/RESUME_CLAIMS.md from those artifacts and tests/test_writeup.py fails on drift. There is no web app, live feed or deployment, by design. Every published number comes from a repo command and a committed artifact in results/.
currentGoals: Mostly-zero items (>= 75% zero days, about 31% of forecast rows) are forecast about 24% too low by both boosted models (docs/RESULTS.md, 'Where the models are weak'): propose a model or feature that targets that segment, for example a Croston-type method or a boosted hurdle model, compared on that segment and on overall WRMSSE

Sudden demand jumps are missed because every sales input is at least 28 days old: propose faster-reacting forecasts, for example a separate model per forecast day with lags as recent as one day, with the leakage tests extended to cover them
One store only: the pipeline already takes --store, so propose extending the evaluation beyond CA_1 in a way the owner can actually run and review
Close the other gaps docs/RESULTS.md names under 'What is not shown' and 'What would come next': prediction intervals, new items forecast from similar items, more folds for an error bar
Checks that could stay green while the thing they guard breaks: a test, leakage check or generated-region check that would not catch its failure

A proposal that would move a published result must say so in its title with [needs-regen] and include the before/after it expects to measure; the loop's runners cannot run m5-backtest (about 18 GB peak memory, GitHub runners have 16 GB), so the owner's crew regenerates the artifacts locally before merge
offLimits: Skipping, deselecting, xfailing or loosening any test or gate (ruff, mypy, pytest, tests/test_leakage.py, tests/test_writeup.py) to get green
Hand-editing GENERATED regions in README.md, docs/RESULTS.md or docs/RESUME_CLAIMS.md, or any file in results/; rerun the command that writes it instead

Fabricated, synthetic or substituted data or reference values: provenance/m5_data.json hashes, the documented M5 facts in src/m5/config.py, and published numbers never come from the synthetic test fixture
Tuning or selecting models toward a target in docs/PLAN.md or docs/RESUME_CLAIMS.md; targets are not results, report what is measured
Features that use sales newer than 28 days before the forecast day, or prices and calendar fields after it, unless the leakage tests are extended to prove the new rule
A web app, live data feed or deployment (docs/PLAN.md non-goals)

Loop machinery: .github/workflows/ (the loop's token cannot push workflow changes; proposals that need one are left for the owner's crew), .github/loop-config.json, the docs/archive/loop-brief.md path, scripts/loop-metrics.mjs, metrics/
Credentials, secrets, money, git history rewrites; AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .claude/
lenses: Forecast weak spots: a segment, series or day type where the committed artifacts show the models are biased or wrong, and a concrete, testable way to do better on it.
Published-claim integrity: a number or statement in README.md or docs/ that its committed artifact in results/ or the code contradicts, or that overstates what was measured.
Checks that cannot fail: a test or gate that would stay green if the leakage rule, the metric, the data verification or the write-up generator broke.
Reviewer's first minute: what a data-science or supply-chain recruiter sees first in the README and docs/RESULTS.md, and where it confuses, buries or oversells the strongest true result.
